commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG user stories for TutorTrack
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide lists AB3's address-book user stories, which
describe managing generic contacts rather than a private tutor's
student roster.

The DG must cover the full requirements of TutorTrack, including
stories considered but not planned, so readers can see the scope
of the product and the priority of each feature.

Replace the AB3 stories with TutorTrack's user stories:

* must-have stories for adding, listing, viewing, noting, and
  deleting students, plus duplicate checks and saving
* nice-to-have stories for editing, finding, undo, help, and
  sample data
* unlikely stories for archiving, sibling linking, note editing,
  and multi-computer access, kept to show what was considered

Use one term for each concept, such as roster, student, parent
contact, and session note, so that no two stories describe the
same thing in different words.

Two user stories in the Developer Guide have weak wording. One
uses the British spelling "misspelt", while the rest of the guide
uses American spelling. Another has a benefit, "see all my
students again", that only restates its want of returning to the
full roster.

A benefit that repeats its want, and inconsistent spelling, are
flagged as user story and documentation bugs during grading.

Use the American spelling "misspelled", and give the return-to-
roster story a distinct benefit: selecting any student by their
roster number again.

TutorTrack has no way to represent what happened in a lesson, so
tutors cannot record session notes yet.

Let's add an immutable SessionNote holding the note text and the
OffsetDateTime at which it was recorded. The text is stripped of
surrounding whitespace and must be 1 to 500 printable characters on
one line, with internal spaces kept as typed.

Length is counted in code points so that an emoji counts as one
character. The caller supplies the timestamp, which keeps the type
deterministic to test and leaves timestamping to the model.

Each student needs an ordered record of their session notes, with
the most recent note easy to find.

Let's add an immutable SessionHistory that keeps notes newest first.
withNote(...) returns a new history and leaves the original
unchanged, so the model can prepare a change before saving it.

Notes are ordered by instant rather than by clock reading, so notes
recorded with different time-zone offsets still sort correctly.
Notes with equal instants keep the order in which they were added.

The Developer Guide does not describe the session note types, and
the design tree still lists the timestamp source as an open
decision.

Let's describe SessionNote and SessionHistory in the Developer
Guide, and record the timestamp decision as settled: the system
date-time with its offset, ordered by instant.

Session histories need a home in the model, but the student roster
does not own session-note data, and keeping a history inside Student
would change Student equality every time a note is added.

Let's add StudentSessionHistories, which maps each StudentId to that
student's SessionHistory. It adds notes, returns an empty history for
students without notes, and removes a history while reporting how
many notes it held.

Keeping the map in its own class, as UniquePersonList does for
persons, lets AddressBook delegate to it instead of growing another
set of rules.

AddressBook holds the roster but has no session notes, so notes
cannot be stored, copied, or compared with the rest of the data.

Let's keep a StudentSessionHistories in AddressBook and expose each
student's history through ReadOnlyAddressBook. A note for a student
who is not in the roster is rejected, so every history belongs to an
existing student. resetData, equals, and hashCode now include the
histories, so copies of the address book keep their notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add session note operations to Model
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands need a way to add, read, and remove session notes, and the
roster still reports zero notes for every student.

Let's add addSessionNote, getSessionHistory, and
removeSessionHistory to Model, and have getStudentRoster supply each
student's real note count.

ModelManager timestamps new notes with an injected Clock, truncated
to whole seconds, so that callers only pass text and tests can use a
fixed time. The existing constructors keep using the system clock.

The Developer Guide and ADR 0003 still say that roster note counts
are always zero, and the architecture notes do not name the
session-note API.

Let's describe how the model stores and exposes session histories,
note that ADR 0003's zero-count limitation is resolved, and list the
Model session-note methods as that context's entry point.

Session notes exist only in memory, so they are lost when TutorTrack
closes.

Let's add JsonAdaptedSessionNote to convert a session note to and
from JSON, with the timestamp stored as an ISO-8601 date-time and
offset. The timestamp is always written with seconds, which
OffsetDateTime#toString leaves out when they are zero, so saved files
read consistently.

Loading rejects a missing field, invalid note text, or a timestamp
without an offset, so a malformed note cannot silently become valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Persist session notes with each student
commitResults.messageBody:
The data file stores students but not their session notes, so notes
added in one session would be lost after a restart.

Let's save each student's notes in a sessionNotes list inside that
student's JSON record, and add them back to the address book when
loading. Keeping notes inside each student's record makes the file
easy to read and edit by hand, while the model still keeps
histories separate from Student.

A missing sessionNotes field loads as an empty history, so existing
data files keep working. An empty or invalid note is a load error,
the same as an invalid student field.

The Developer Guide does not describe how session notes are stored
in the data file.

Let's document the sessionNotes JSON layout, why notes are nested in
each student's record, the timestamp format, and how missing or
malformed notes are handled when loading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add note command for session notes
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors can see each student's note count, but have no way to record
what happened in a lesson.

Let's add `note INDEX nt/NOTE`, which adds a timestamped session note
to the student at INDEX in the roster and reports the student's name.
The index is resolved against the same sorted roster that `list`
shows, and the note is stored by the student's ID.

Only nt/ is recognized, so text such as "sub/" stays part of the
note. A missing or invalid index is reported as an invalid command
format, as `delete` does. NoteCommand#toString leaves out the note
text, which may contain private lesson details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the note workflow end to end
commitResults.messageBody:
Unit tests cover the note parser, command, model, and storage
separately, but not whether a typed note survives a restart.

Let's add an integration test that runs `add` and `note` through
LogicManager with real JSON storage, reloads the saved file, and
checks the notes, their order, timestamps, and roster counts. It
also checks that rejected `note` commands leave the data file
unchanged.

The User Guide does not mention `note`, still says roster note
counts are always zero, and does not explain how notes appear in the
data file. The Developer Guide has no design notes or manual tests
for the command.

Let's describe `note` in the User Guide with its format, rules,
examples, and errors, add it to the command summary, and explain the
sessionNotes format for users who edit the data file. In the
Developer Guide, describe how the command parses input, resolves the
index, and saves the note, and add manual-testing steps.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore data when saving a command fails
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager saves the address book after a command changes the
model, but keeps the change when saving fails. The user is told the
command failed, yet the change stays in memory and is written to the
file by the next successful save. The API contract requires a failed
save to leave the model unchanged.

Let's copy the address book before running each command and restore
the copy if saving fails, then report the same error as before.

Restoring in LogicManager covers every command, including add, note,
and delete, without each command having to undo its own changes. The
storage-failure test in LogicManagerTest now expects the model to be
unchanged, matching the contract.

The guides do not say what happens to the data when saving fails.

Let's describe the copy-and-restore step in the Developer Guide,
including the alternative of per-command undo and the remaining risk
of a partly written file. Tell users in the User Guide that a
command is cancelled when its changes cannot be saved, and record
the decision in the design tree.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#82] Reject duplicate student IDs when loading data #101
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file with two students sharing a studentId loaded without

and the app failed to start. The two students would also have shared
session notes, as notes are stored by student ID.

Treat a repeated studentId as a load error in
JsonSerializableAddressBook, so the app starts with an empty address
book instead of crashing. Add a test data file with duplicate IDs,
and note in the User Guide that each studentId must be unique.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#80] Keep invalid data files instead of overwriting them (#100)
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file failed to load, TutorTrack started with an empty
address book and only logged a warning. The next command then saved
over the file, so one invalid record could wipe the whole roster and
all session notes.

Copy an unreadable data file to a uniquely named backup beside it at
startup, before any command can save, and show an error dialog that
says where the copy was kept. Document the recovery steps in the User
Guide and Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align session note Javadoc and names with SE-EDU
commitResults.messageBody:
Parts of the session note code do not follow the SE-EDU Java coding
standard. Several @throws descriptions start with a lowercase "if",
two helper methods have noun names, two lines exceed the 110-char
soft limit, and two non-trivial private methods lack header comments.

Let's capitalize the @throws descriptions, rename missingField and
studentId to createMissingFieldException and createStudentId, rewrap
the long lines, and add the missing header comments.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix list formatting in User and Developer Guides
commitResults.messageBody:
The note examples list in the User Guide has no blank line before it,
and the Logic component steps in the Developer Guide are numbered 1 to
5. The SE-EDU Markdown standard asks for a blank line before every list
and for 1. on every ordered-list item.

Let's add the blank line and number every Logic step 1.

commitResults.messageTitle: Log only the command word of user commands
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager logs the full text of every command, and MainWindow logs
the full text of a command that fails. AddressBookParser also logs the
arguments at FINE and the full input of an unknown command at FINER.
Parent phone numbers and emails from add, and lesson notes from note,
therefore end up in the log file, which the coding policy forbids.

Let's log at most the command word, such as [USER COMMAND][note], in
all four places. A first word that is not a known command is logged
as "unknown", since a mistyped command may start with a student's
name or phone number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Logging guide: Explain how to log user commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Developers adding log statements have no guidance on which parts of

Let's point them to AddressBookParser#getLoggableCommandWord and
explain why the full command text must not be logged.

Git does not enable the hooks in .beryl/githooks when the repository

Let's explain how to enable the hooks in the DevOps guide, and update

commitResults.messageTitle: Document private helpers in note parsing and rollback
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager#restore and NoteCommandParser#parseIndex are non-trivial
private methods without header comments, and parseIndex names its
caught exception "pe" while the rest of the session note code uses
"exception".

Let's add header comments to both methods and rename the variable to
match the coding standard's example.

The session note code relies on invariants that nothing checks:
histories are ordered newest first, an added note appears in its
student's history, and every persisted note is loaded back.

Let's state them as assertions so that a bug breaking any of them
fails fast in development and tests, instead of corrupting the
history silently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplicated setup in model and logic tests
commitResults.messageBody:
ModelTest builds the same address book with ALEX and INDICES_NOTE in
two tests, and four LogicManagerTest save-failure tests repeat the
same model setup.

Let's extract the setup into helper methods so each test shows only
what differs.

Obsolete MVP planning documents and the standalone PR-review notes
remain in the repository, so agents load outdated context and cannot
discover the review guidance.

Let's remove the MVP specification files, move the review guidance
into a reviewing-prs Beryl skill registered in every tool shim, and
keep the commit-message conventions in one section of the coding
policy.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#130] Tighten up behavior of add function (#132)
commitResults.messageBody:
The add command reports vague messages, silently absorbs unknown
prefixes such as x/value into the level, and can leave an empty data
file behind when the first save fails.

Let's report each failure as the problem followed by the add usage,
reject unknown lower-case prefixes while still accepting subjects such
as "E Math/A Math", and create the data file only through the atomic
write so a failed first save leaves no file behind.

The repository has a Markdownlint configuration and the agent policies
tell developers to run it, but there is no package.json, so the command
cannot run, and the configured rules do not fully match the SE-EDU
Markdown standard.

Let's add markdownlint-cli2 as a locked local dev dependency, document
the setup step, scope every documented command to changed files with
--no-globs, and enforce ATX headings and 1. numbering for ordered
lists. Markdownlint stays out of CI and Git hooks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Number same-second session notes in added order
commitResults.messageBody:
Session notes are timestamped to whole seconds. When two notes for a
student share a timestamp, SessionHistory places the note added later
below the earlier one, so it is shown as older and gets the lower
note number. The UG promises that [1] is the oldest note, and
"delete note" can then remove a different note from the one intended.

Let's,
* treat a newly added note as the newest among notes with an equal
  timestamp
* restore saved histories in their saved order through a new
  SessionHistory#of, instead of re-adding each note with withNote
* add AddressBook#setSessionHistory so loading sets each history once

Re-adding saved notes one by one would treat each later-loaded note
as newer and reverse same-second notes on every reload. Building the
history from the saved list with a stable sort keeps their order,
while hand-edited files that are out of order still load sorted.

Tests that relied on the old tie order now expect the note added
later to be listed first.

The DG says notes with equal instants keep the order in which they
were added, and that loading re-adds each saved note through
AddressBook#addSessionNote. Neither is true once same-second notes
are numbered in added order.

Let's describe how SessionHistory orders same-second notes and how
loading restores a saved history, and update the matching design-tree
entry.

commitResults.messageTitle: Skip saving when a command changes no data
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager saves the data file after every command other than
deletions, including commands that change nothing, such as view, help
and exit. When saving fails, those commands fail with the save error,
so the user cannot open a profile or the help window, or exit with
the exit command. If the data file failed to load and could not be
backed up, running help or view also overwrites it with an empty
roster.

The save error also names the temporary file used for the write
rather than the data file, which confuses the user.

Let's,
* skip saving when the address book is unchanged after a command
* name the data file in both save error messages

Comparing the address book with the copy already taken for rollback
covers every command, including future ones, without each command
having to declare whether it changes data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document skipping saves for unchanged data
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG says every command on the persistence path is saved, and that
a failed save reports the storage exception's message. Neither is
true once commands that change no data skip saving and save errors
name the data file.

Let's describe both in the logic flow and the save-failure rollback
section.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a specific error for invalid note indices
commitResults.messageBody:
NoteCommandParser reports every index problem as an invalid command
format. For input in the right format whose index is wrong, such as
"note 0 nt/text" or "note x nt/text", the user is told the format is
wrong instead of what is wrong with the index.

Let's report that INDEX must be a positive integer when the text
before nt/ is a single word that is not a positive integer, and keep
the format error for an empty or multi-word preamble.

This matches how "delete note" reports its invalid indices, so both
note commands give the same kind of error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the invalid note index error
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG says the note command reports an invalid index as an invalid
command format, and its manual testing steps expect that error for
"note 0 nt/text" and "note x nt/text". Neither is true once invalid
indices get their own message.

Let's describe the new error in the note command section and give it
its own manual testing step.

AddressBook#resetData replaced the persons with one setter call, then
reset the students and rebuilt the session histories inline. Mixing
these levels of abstraction made readers trace the loop to see that it
only copies each student's history.

Extract the student reset and the session-history copy into private
setters, so resetData reads as three steps at the same level. Behavior
is unchanged.
